subject: health
title: Correction and reflection: teasing, bullying, and reporting
essentialQuestion: How do respectful words and clear boundaries keep me and my friendships safe?
keyPoints: Bullying is deliberate, repeated, and aimed at someone who is finding it hard to stop it.
It can be physical, spoken, social such as deliberate exclusion, or online.
A bystander who tells an adult, includes the person afterwards, or refuses to join in changes the outcome.
Reporting bullying is telling to keep someone safe; it is not tattling.
privacySafeScenario: The same group leaves one classmate out of every game and laughs when they walk past. Is this bullying? What can a bystander do?
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about teasing, bullying, and reporting to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: Name one thing you corrected or would do differently, and one other place teasing, bullying, and reporting would be useful.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about teasing, bullying, and reporting.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: Scripts may be spoken, signed, typed, drawn as a comic, or acted with figures or puppets. Role-play is optional and may always be replaced by describing what a character should say.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about teasing, bullying, and reporting under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, agree on the family rule for secrets and who is always safe to tell. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
